A first stop before [Classic Organs Compared](organ-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Continental is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Vox Continental** is a transistor *combo organ*, first made in **1962** at the Jennings factory in Dartford, Kent (Wikipedia, "Vox Continental").
- It has twelve oscillators, one for each note of the top octave; frequency dividers halve them for every octave below (Wikipedia).
- Its keys are reverse-coloured: black naturals, white sharps, "as on a harpsichord" (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- **Six drawbars**: four for the footages 16′, 8′, 4′ and **IV** (a mixture of higher pitches), two for the voices, flute and reed (Wikipedia).
- The voice drawbars colour **every** footage at once.
- One **vibrato**, "single-speed, single-intensity" (Wikipedia).
- No percussion, no Leslie of its own, no second manual.

## The panel

This is the Continental panel from [Classic Organs Compared](organ-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). Play it from the keys under the panel or the computer keys (a w s e d f t g y h u j k); **Keys play** picks the manual. Pull a drawbar or press a tab while you play. The sound is this site's own model; nobody has compared it with the real instrument.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a registration and plays the same short phrase.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vox-bright" data-set="{&quot;d4&quot;:0,&quot;dIV&quot;:0,&quot;reed&quot;:0,&quot;flute&quot;:8}"><p><b>8′, flute only.</b> Listen: a soft, plain tone.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vox-bright" data-set="{&quot;d4&quot;:0,&quot;dIV&quot;:0,&quot;flute&quot;:0}"><p><b>8′, reed only.</b> Listen: buzzier, more nasal.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vox-bright" data-set="{&quot;dIV&quot;:0}"><p><b>Add the 4′.</b> Listen: brighter, an octave up added.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vox-bright"><p><b>Add IV.</b> The mixture adds high pitches. Listen: thin and cutting.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vox-lmf"><p><b>Vibrato on.</b> A blend of flute and reed with the vibrato: a starting point for "Light My Fire".</p></div>
```

## Build it from a record

Each record below has a **Build it on the panel** button that loads a *starting* registration made on this page (not the player's documented setting), so you can listen to the record and change the panel by ear until it is close.

```{=html}
<div class="ocmp-tracks" data-organ="vox"></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Vox Continental":

- The Animals, "The House of the Rising Sun" (Alan Price)
- The Doors, "Light My Fire" (Ray Manzarek)
- ? and the Mysterians, "96 Tears"
- The Beatles, "I'm Down" (live) and "Think for Yourself"

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How does the Continental make its notes?</b></p><ul><li>Top-octave oscillators divided down</li><li>Tonewheels</li><li>Pipes</li><li>Samples</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Twelve oscillators and frequency dividers.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What do the two right-hand drawbars do?</b></p><ul><li>Set the voice: flute and reed</li><li>Change the key</li><li>Speed up a Leslie</li><li>Add reverb</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What is odd about its keys?</b></p><ul><li>Black naturals, white sharps</li><li>They are round</li><li>There are only 12</li><li>They are touch-sensitive</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Reverse-coloured.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How many vibrato speeds does it have?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Three</li><li>Six</li><li>None</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Single speed, single intensity.</p></div>
```
